focus: Adaptive Hierarchical Depth Selection via Capability Composition
question: Will a prospectively deployed adaptive depth‑selection policy, derived offline by selecting the depth that minimized observed error for each horizon, achieve higher expected utility (i.e., lower average planning error) than any single fixed‑depth policy on a held‑out set of planning tasks?
hypothesis: When evaluated on a held‑out set of planning tasks, the adaptive policy will produce a statistically lower average planning error than the best static depth policy identified from the same observational data, yielding a positive approximated G_A (difference in expected utility between the two interventions).
next_action: Interpret the latest evidence, update the open hypothesis, and choose the next bounded step.
